title: Open immersions descend along qcqs affine-transition limits
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty directed set and $(S_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes with affine transition morphisms [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] [pqf-def-affine-morphism], and let $S=\varprojlim_iS_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Fix $i_0\in I$, quasi-compact quasi-separated $S_{i_0}$-schemes $X_{i_0},Y_{i_0}$, and an $S_{i_0}$-morphism $f_{i_0}:X_{i_0}\to Y_{i_0}$ locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Write $f_i$ and $f$ for its base changes to $S_i$ and $S$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. If $f$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], there is $i\geq i_0$ such that $f_j$ is an open immersion for every $j\geq i$. No affineness of $X_{i_0}$ or $Y_{i_0}$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0EUU, label lemma-descend-open-immersion, in Situation situation-descent-property; persistence by base change of open immersions

proof.text: The limit morphism $f$ is étale and a monomorphism, since it is an open immersion. These are properties of the entire morphism, with no affineness hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0EUU, lemma-descend-open-immersion; open-immersion étaleness and monicity

proof.text: Local finite presentation implies locally finite type by the instance in Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.FinitePresentation, which applies RingHom.FiniteType.of_finitePresentation on affine pairs. Thus the locally finite type hypothesis of monomorphism descent is available without constructing affine covers.

source.place: Tag 01TQ, lemma-locally-finite-presentation-characterize; finite presentation implies finite generation

proof.text: Apply étale descent to the original $S_{i_0}$-morphism: $S_{i_0},X_{i_0},Y_{i_0}$ are qcqs, transition morphisms are affine, the limit map is étale by step 1, and the original map is locally of finite presentation by hypothesis. Obtain $a\geq i_0$ with $f_a$ étale. Independently apply monomorphism descent to the same original morphism, using step 2 for locally finite type and step 1 for monicity at the limit. Obtain $b\geq i_0$ with $f_b$ monic.

Choose i >= a,b by directedness, and fix any j >= i. For c = a or b, put p:S_c -> S_i0 and q:S_j -> S_c. For any morphism X0 -> Y0 over S_i0, the square from its base change along q followed by p to its base change along p is cartesian. To prove this, first cancel the base-change square for Y0 from the square for X0; this gives the base-change square of the morphism. Then cancel the resulting square at c from the square at j. The comparison maps are the pullback maps induced by the identity on X0 or Y0 and q on the base. Their commutativity is checked on both pullback projections. Functoriality of D and uniqueness of morphisms in the preorder identify q followed by p with the transition from j to i0.

source.place: Tag 02GO, lemma-base-change-etale; elementary pullback cancellation and associativity

proof.text: Use the cartesian square from step 4 for c = a to transfer etaleness of f_a to f_j by base-change stability. Use it for c = b to transfer monicity: after equalizing the projection to Y_j, monicity of f_b equalizes the projection to X_b, and the pullback universal property equalizes the maps. Thus f_j is etale and monic.

source.place: Tag 02GO, lemma-base-change-etale; elementary pullback cancellation for monomorphisms

proof.text: A monomorphism is universally injective: its diagonal is an isomorphism, hence surjective, and the diagonal criterion in def-weil-radicial-morphism applies. Therefore f_j is universally injective. The radicial-etale recognition theorem makes f_j an open immersion. Since j >= i was arbitrary, the conclusion holds at every later stage.

F1 formalization uses Mathlib finite-presentation-to-finite-type inference and cartesian-square cancellation to transfer both properties directly to each later stage.
